historic_survey.survey: Early Settlement Era Styles Historic Context Statement (2025)
historic_survey.note: The Old United States Mint, San Francisco Landmark No. 236 — the statement's chosen exemplar of Greek Revival in the Bay Area, and the style at its most legible: large columns and pediments, often with elaborate friezes, and often intact.

historical_record.description: The most prominent building in the area to survive the fire intact, with thick stone and brick walls, cast iron fire shutters, internal fire suppression reservoirs and a workforce that put out every fire that entered the building.
One of only two Treasury Section of Fine Arts commissions completed in San Francisco: a series of bronze eagle reliefs by Albert Stewart, of which one survives.

Architects Mario Ciampi and Allyn Martin presented plans to redevelop the site as 'Gold Plaza', an urban park surrounded by modern office towers, with only the Mint's columns left standing. The opposition the plan aroused led to the Mint's designation as a National Historic Landmark in 1961.

unknowns: The city's statement on early settlement era styles dates the building twice and disagrees with itself: its landmark list and illustration caption give 1874, its statement of significance about 1869.
